summary: Licence flow-down obligation from the MiniMax H3 authorization needs a user consent gate in front of a licence-gated model download. Blocks shipping H3; does not block MPI-449 bench research.

Generalised from an H3-only consent gate to a reusable licence-gate system driven by a ModelDef descriptor; Flux named as the next consumer. Design settled: territory-restricted licences route the user to the licensor's own authorization form rather than disclaiming responsibility onto them. Marked as blocking MPI-452.

todo -> doing. Gate hooks downloadService.start() (five install call sites, one chokepoint); non-gated models keep the synchronous download:started emit MpiModelManager._install depends on. Descriptors in js/data/modelConstants/licences.js keyed by model id, not on the ModelDef. Scroll-to-bottom gates the Use Restrictions + Exhibit A pane; the full 17KB agreement is a link out. Discord is the misuse-reporting route.

Built and self-verified; maturity in-progress -> validating. Gate hooks downloadService.start(); ungated models proved to still reach _start in the SAME TICK, which MpiModelManager._install depends on. All seven acceptance criteria evidenced in validation.md. Three defects the source could not show were found by driving the real dialog in Chromium: a scroll gate computed before layout is always satisfied and shipped the checkboxes unlocked; clientLogger.log does not exist and its throw left the install promise pending forever; and the dialog overflowed a 720px viewport, pushing the buttons off screen. Standing licence + misuse-reporting route added to the model detail drawer for gated models only. OPEN: the H3 model id is owned by the MPI-452 session and a mismatch is a SILENT no-gate.

MPI-452 confirmed the ModelDef id is minimax-h3 - descriptor key was already correct, no re-key. They also flagged that reference-to-video ships as a SEPARATE ModelDef minimax-h3-ref2va under the same agreement; I took that key rather than leaving it for their ModelDef, so licences.js stays one owner's file. Both ids now point at one hoisted descriptor const. That exposed a wrong assumption in the original shape: receipts keyed by MODEL id would have shown the same 25 clauses twice for one agreement, so receipts now key on the LICENCE id - a deliberate deviation from the card's 'recorded per model' wording, which predates the two-ModelDef fact. Reasoning and the one-line revert are in validation.md. 459 tests pass; shared acceptance verified live through the chokepoint.
